title: Michael Ben-Or
name: Michael Ben-Or
summary: Theoretical computer scientist whose work spans fault-tolerant distributed computation, secure multiparty computation, cryptography, and quantum computing.
whyThisMatters: Michael Ben-Or is included for documented contributions to the technical and formal foundations of computer security and cryptography.

sections.overview:
Michael Ben-Or is a computer scientist associated with the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. His research addresses how computation can remain correct and private despite failures or adversarial behavior.

Security relevance

Ben-Or’s work on distributed agreement and secure multiparty computation provided rigorous constructions for collaboration among parties that may be faulty or malicious. It is a key bridge between distributed-systems reliability and cryptographic privacy.

timeline.event: Receives a Ph.D. in mathematics from the Hebrew University.
Publishes work on completely asynchronous agreement.
Co-authors a foundational paper on fault-tolerant distributed computation.
Co-authors work on fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant error rate.
